themes.title: China's rare-earth suspension expires Tuesday Nov 10 — the two published dates conflict
themes.description: MOFCOM's Sept 28 statement extended the US trade arrangement to Jan 10, 2027, yet Announcement No. 70, the legal notice suspending the October 2025 controls, still says Nov 10 and no numbered extension had appeared as of Nov 7. April 2025 licensing on seven elements remains either way. Western equities already sit near lows, so a clean extension is not priced as upside and a lapse is partly priced as downside.

themes.title: GM's termination of its VAC South Carolina magnet deal is still the key anchor-customer warning
themes.description: GM cancelled a 2023 supply agreement for e-VAC's ~$500M, ~2,000t/yr South Carolina plant (VAC has launched arbitration), and Energy Fuels' $1.9B VAC purchase price may adjust. MP's contrast case improved this week: it completed GM magnet qualification with saleable deliveries and revenue starting in Q4, though its Magnetics segment revenue was just $18.6M.

themes.title: Juniors keep funding through equity and mergers while prices stay low
themes.description: Energy Fuels' $500M at-the-market programme (shares fell ~10% on the news) and law-firm probes continue with the stock near $7.56; USAR filed a $1.25B shelf in September and reports Nov 9; Critical Metals' European Lithium acquisition cleared the WA Supreme Court Oct 26. Equity is still the funding tool while prices are low.

themes.title: Lynas posts a record NdPr quarter on prices — but December-quarter maintenance and a weak share price temper it
themes.description: Lynas' September quarter showed gross revenue A$310.1M (+55%), record NdPr output of 2,082t, and an average selling price of A$102.1/kg (+88%), with price floors covering over half of production and a US$96M Pentagon R&D oxide arrangement; sales volume fell 17.7% and planned Malaysia/Kalgoorlie maintenance will weigh on the December quarter. Ord Minnett cut to Hold (A$13.50) while BMO initiated at Outperform (A$17). Figures come from a secondary summary, not Lynas's own filing.

bear_case.title: The premium keeps deflating faster than the supply chain is built
bear_case.description: REMX ~$51.40 (Nov 6) is -17% over a month, MP at $35.41 is down ~24% over a month despite a Q3 beat (Magnetics revenue still only $18.6M), USAR hit $8.89 and Lynas A$10.71. MP remains loss-making; the GM/VAC cancellation shows Western magnet capacity can lose anchor demand even with policy support.

bear_case.title: Commodity cycles cut both ways
bear_case.description: Lithium carbonate is ~25% lower in a month at CNY 93,600/t and Albemarle itself guides Q4 down on lower pricing despite a blowout Q3 — peak-earnings risk. Copper fell ~6% in a month to ~$6.25/lb and Freeport ($59) is ~26% under its 52-week high. A producer can be an excellent business at the wrong point in its price cycle.

bear_case.title: China can flood, freeze or consolidate
bear_case.description: The pause lapses Nov 10 under the legal notice while the political statement says Jan 10 — the conflict itself is the risk. China holds ~69% of mine output and up to ~90% of processing; a flood of cheap NdPr would undercut non-Chinese producers, and price floors protect only projects that already have product. Lynas's record A$102/kg realized price shows how much current earnings depend on floors and premiums.

bear_case.title: Junior dilution, milestone funding and policy dependency
bear_case.description: Energy Fuels' $500M ATM, USAR's $1.25B shelf, Critical Metals' offering registration and going-concern doubt show juniors funding through shares. Vault, EXIM and DoD floors are real but discretionary; no new Project Vault or EXIM developments were confirmed this week.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: MP Materials
positions.note: Q3 revenue +176% to $147.7M, adjusted EPS $0.04 beat, NdPr sales +94% and GM magnet qualification (revenue from Q4) keep it Core, though at $35.41 (-24% in a month) with Magnetics revenue only $18.6M it is held on business quality, not price. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: USA Rare Earth
positions.note: Serra Verde closed Sept 3 and Blacksburg is the next test, but a $8.89 low, a $1.25B shelf filed in September, milestone-based federal funding and a Nov 9 earnings print make this optionality with a genuine chance of zero.

positions.name: Lithium Americas
positions.note: Thacker Pass is still the largest US lithium build, but at ~$2.05 near its $2.02 low with lithium carbonate -25% in a month to CNY 93.6k/t and completion not until late 2027, it stays the smallest position.

positions.name: Freeport-McMoRan
positions.note: Excellent copper business (Q3 adj. EPS $0.88 vs $0.83, 3.7B lb guided for 2027, $4.5B Bagdad expansion), but copper is ~9% under its $6.85 record and fell ~6% in a month, and the Section 232 tariff decision is unresolved — a late-cycle price, not an entry point.

positions.name: Albemarle
positions.note: Q3 adjusted EBITDA +186% to $645.5M is peak-price earnings: Albemarle itself guides Q4 down sequentially on lower pricing while lithium carbonate sits at CNY 93.6k/t (-25% in a month), so the cycle question is still open.

positions.name: Lynas Rare Earths
positions.note: Record NdPr quarter (2,082t, revenue A$310.1M, ASP A$102/kg with floors over half of output) is real, but December-quarter maintenance, Ord Minnett's Hold and a share price at its A$10.71 low keep it a good business with an unresolved question.

positions.name: Energy Fuels
positions.note: A $500M at-the-market programme (shares ~-10%), law-firm probes and GM's termination of the VAC plant's supply deal (arbitration, $1.9B price possibly adjusting) put dilution and deal-risk ahead of a still-unprofitable ramp at $7.56.

positions.name: Critical Metals
positions.note: Substantial going-concern doubt and no producing asset, plus a recent offering registration; the European Lithium approval (Oct 26) and Tanbreez permit are real but the research does not support owning it at ~$6.38.
